title: AI Examples
description: Small Artificial Intelligence examples from the lessons. Each example links back to its explanation and practice task.

examples.title: What an AI task looks like
examples.description: Artificial intelligence, or AI, is a broad area of computing. It includes programs that search for plans or use data to make predictions. Different tasks need different methods.
examples.code:
Task: help find a library book
Input: a title typed by a learner
Output: matching titles
Check: compare with the real catalogue

examples.title: Use an explicit rule
examples.description: A rule tells a program exactly what to do when a condition is met. Some AI systems include rules, while others learn patterns from data.

examples.title: Represent a problem as states
examples.description: A state is a description of the current situation. An action changes one state into another. A goal describes the state we want to reach.
examples.code:
Start state: at classroom
Action: walk to corridor
Next state: at corridor
Action: walk to library
Goal state: at library

examples.title: Store connected places
examples.description: A graph stores things and their connections. We can describe school rooms with a dictionary whose lists name directly connected rooms.

examples.title: Search one step at a time
examples.description: Breadth-first search checks nearer places before farther places. A queue holds places still waiting to be checked.

examples.title: A helpful guess can guide search
examples.description: A heuristic is a useful estimate that guides search. A straight-line distance can suggest which place is nearer, but it may ignore walls or closed paths.
examples.code:
Route A: looks short on a map, but a gate is closed
Route B: looks longer, and all paths are open
Next check: verify which moves are allowed

examples.title: Respect all constraints
examples.description: A constraint is a rule every allowed answer must satisfy. A timetable needs a free room and an available teacher at the same time.

examples.title: Rules and learned patterns
examples.description: A rule-based program follows rules written by people. A learned model finds patterns using examples. Both need testing and can make mistakes.
examples.code:
Written rule: a book is long if pages > 200
Learned model: use labelled book examples to choose a pattern
Check: compare decisions with the task definition

examples.title: Uncertainty deserves a number
examples.description: Uncertainty means we do not know the outcome for sure. A past fraction can describe observed results, but a small sample gives weak evidence about the future.

examples.title: Agents observe and act
examples.description: An agent is a system that observes a situation and chooses an action. It needs clear allowed actions and a way to check what happened.
examples.code:
Observe: shelf count is zero
Suggest: ask when a book may return
Human checks: is the shelf count current?
Allowed action in this demo: show a suggestion

examples.title: Check who the data represents
examples.description: A dataset is a collection of examples. If some groups or situations are missing, a model may work unevenly. Check results for the people and conditions it will serve.
examples.code:
Sample: only clear photos in bright daylight
Planned use: photos in daylight and dim rooms
Missing check: results on suitable dim-room examples

examples.title: Keep a person able to review
examples.description: An AI result should be easy to question and correct. For important choices, people need the evidence, limits and a way to reject a poor suggestion.
examples.code:
Suggestion: choose route B
Evidence: route A has a closed gate
Limit: map was checked yesterday
Review: confirm the gate and path are still safe
